description: The figure is a multi-level pie (sunburst) chart representing the distribution of medical-ethics topics, organized into four main principles and their associated subtopics. The inner ring shows 4 primary slices: a large blue slice for Beneficence (roughly about half of the circle), a green slice for Autonomy (about a quarter), a purple slice for Non-Maleficence (around a sixth), and an orange slice for Justice (around a tenth). The outer ring subdivides these into 24 labeled sub-slices total (6 per principle), with each sub-slice shown in a lighter tint of its parent color and appearing approximately equal in size within each principle: Beneficence (light blue) includes “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Provide Assistance in Emergency,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” and “Comply with Laws and Regulations”; Autonomy (light green) includes “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” “Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives,” “Keep Confidential of Patient’s Information,” “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication,” and “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice”; Non-Maleficence (light purple) includes “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain,” plus two additional similarly sized light-purple slices with smaller text; and Justice (light orange) includes “Promote the Health of Community and Public Education,” “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally,” plus two additional similarly sized light-orange slices with smaller text. There is no separate legend and no numeric percentage labels printed inside slices; labels are written directly on the wedges, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized beyond color grouping.
